procedure.step: The exporter applies for the Certificate of Origin for India through the e-service: logs in, completes the form, uploads proof of factory registration, commercial invoice, and for a trading exporter the factory's purchase invoice, pays the fee online, and submits.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade charges a certificate fee of AED 50 for invoice value up to AED 100000.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade issues the preferential certificate of origin.
Processing takes about one working day; the service runs 24/7.
The competent authority ensures the certificate is issued before, at, or within five working days of export; it is valid for twelve months from issue and covers only one import.
The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry, uploads the certificate to e-Sanchit, and keeps supporting documents for at least five years from filing.
The exporter keeps origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least five years from the end of the calendar year of issue.

caveats.note: Estimate on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.

CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) and the Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Cess (AIDC) for lines in Table II; IGST, GST compensation cess, the Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
'+' in a rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Indian inputs count as originating only with proof of their originating status (bilateral cumulation, Art. 3.7).
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
By interpretation, de minimis helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the VA percentage.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
Factory registration requires the factory to be located outside a free zone; a producer in a free zone is likely not eligible.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum record retention; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.
The certificate fee assumes the certificate's invoice value equals the shipment value given.
An issued certificate can be amended once for a fee of AED 20; the invoice amount and the destination cannot be changed.
